messages:
maria: quick thread — swapped FP8 -> INT8 kernels on a prod-like trace for llama-13B. avg throughput +12% but p95 latency worsened ~18%. wondering if kv warmup / batching heuristics flipped kernel choices mid-request :thinking:

kevin: saw something similar. profiler shows KV miss rate jumped at prefix lengths > 64, and kernel selector moved to a different matmul path. short log snippet: 
```
# before (FP8)
p50: 90ms, p95: 220ms, throughput: 120 req/s
# after (INT8)
p50: 85ms, p95: 260ms, throughput: 135 req/s
kv_miss_rate: 0.08 -> 0.18
```

perf-bot: automated-profile-summary: link=https://perf/reports/1745123045 (samples: 12k, workload: prod-spike-2025-03). Top regressions: kernel_swap_matmul_fast->matmul_int8_block (p95 +17%). KV cache hotness decreased in 3/5 shard mixes.

sophia: my hypothesis — calibration set used for INT8 was mostly short, chat-like prompts. INT8 per-channel calibration is more sensitive to tail tokens and outliers; if we used per-tensor it might be more robust for the long-tail but worse for average. we should also consider percentile clipping on activations (e.g., 99.5 vs 99.9).

raj: also worth checking batching heuristics: our selector switches kernel at batch_size >= 6 and seq_len distributions were bimodal. if many requests get coalesced into medium batches it can pick a kernel optimized for bigger batches but that hurts p95 for small interactive sessions. maybe change the threshold or add latency SLO bias.

jason: config I ran for calibration (INT8, per-channel, 99.9 clip): 
```
quant_config:
  mode: int8
  granularity: per_channel
  clip_percentile: 99.9
  outlier_trim: 0.001
```

dmitri: reproducer for the KV warmup spike: run this local trace and watch `kv_cache_miss_ratio` and `kernel_choice` logs. command: `./tools/run_trace --trace prod-spike-2025-03 --warmup 2 --batcher coalescing_v2` — note warmup=2 is deliberately low which exaggerates p95.

kevin: quick experiment idea: try per-channel calibrations but force outlier trimming at 0.1% and extend KV warmup to 8 tokens (simulate prefill). expecting p95 to recover ~10-12% while keeping throughput gains. also enable sticky-kernel selection for the first 20 tokens so we don't flip mid-request.

maria: sounds good. I'll schedule two canaries: (A) per-channel + 0.1% trim + warmup 8 + sticky kernel, (B) per-tensor + 99.9 clip + warmup 2. running at 1745126800 and 1745128600. can someone watch the canaries and grab profiler links? :pray:

sophia: I'll watch A. will post perf links and a quick diff. :+1:

kevin: if A looks promising we should also run a calibration set that includes ~5% long-form generation sessions to capture KV tail behavior. otherwise our quant profile will be blind to warmup dynamics.

maria: agreed — adding a long-form slice to calibration set. thanks all, will follow up with results in this thread.
